subject: Post-demo synthesis & interop test plan (vendor bake-off)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@fintechco.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@fintechco.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo synthesis & first-pass criteria

Hi Maya / Liam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick synthesis from our side so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed or want reprioritized.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Latency variability on short conversations (95p spikes to 1.2s vs target <= 400ms).
- Token cost growth as user volume scales — unit economics are a blocker for wider rollout.
- Security/data residency for EU users (auditability + KMS controls).

Goals you set: 
1) Proof of consistent sub-400ms p95 latency for typical chat flows (50–150 tokens).
2) 30–40% reduction in per-session token cost vs current vendor without degrading quality.
3) Clear security artifacts (SOC 2 scope, KMS integration, audit log sampling).

Decision criteria (early draft — attached spreadsheet):
- Latency profile (p50/p95/p99)
- Cost per thousand tokens under realistic batching
- Quality (BLEU-like heuristics + manual eval on 100 prompts)
- Ops maturity (traceability, rerouting, fallback behavior)

Proposed next steps:
- We (Redwood) will run an interop test plan against your sample dataset and a synthetic load to validate latency and cost. Attachment: interop-test-plan.md.
- You to provide a sanitized sample of 1k representative conversations and a procurement contact for security artifacts.
- Sync on schedule: we can start tests next Tue (6/1) if that's OK.

Attachments: interop-test-plan.md (test steps), redwood-bakeoff-criteria.xlsx (scoring rubric).

Thanks — will keep the thread tight and action-oriented.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
From: Maya Patel <maya@fintechco.com>

Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis & first-pass criteria

Sergio — thanks for the crisp recap. This matches our view with a few clarifications:

1) Latency: the 400ms p95 target is for US users only initially; EU will have a looser target (p95 <= 700ms) because of routing constraints.
2) Cost: our finance team wants the comparison both against our current vendor list price and the realized per-session cost over the last quarter (we can share a sample CSV).
3) Security: SOC 2 Type II evidence is required before we move to a closed POC. Also need to confirm that token-level logs can be redacted and stored in our KMS-backed bucket.

We're generally aligned with your test plan but can you add an explicit A/B quality check step (human-rated on N=100) against our current production vendor? That will be decisive.

Procurement contact is Liam O'Connor (cc'd) — he'll handle DOCS / PO questions. We can share the sanitized conversations by Friday.

Maya
Director of Product, FinTechCo
maya@fintechco.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Post-demo synthesis & first-pass criteria — technical notes

Looping in some technical context for the test plan so Maya has concrete expectations.

Proposed technical tests (short):
- Test A: Latency profile under steady-state concurrency (500 qps synthetic with realistic token distribution). Measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
- Test B: Burst recovery test (simulate 2x traffic for 60s then return to baseline). Validate graceful degradation and fallback to smaller model variant.
- Test C: End-to-end A/B quality: duplicate 100 conversational seeds to Redwood and their current vendor; collect blind ratings on accuracy/usefulness from your raters.

Notes on data handling:
- We will run client-side redaction job (open-source script) that replaces account ids and PAN-like artifacts. We will not store raw PII on our side; only hashed ids and trace ids for debugging (per agreement).
- For KMS proofs we can provide a key rotation log and a sample encrypted artifact stored in S3 (we will redact values before sharing).

I'll prepare a short runbook and smoke test harness. Grace, can you confirm headcount for the human eval by Monday?

— Priyom
